title: WorldTUI: I trained a 360M model to pretend to be a terminal
short: WorldTUI: a 360M model that predicts a terminal's screen, keypress by keypress
author: Simon Edwardsson (V7)
more_note: Its videos (vim, tmux, snake, the Python REPL) show the model at its best; the demo is the honest test: open it, try a command it has not seen, and come back to a file three commands later.
takeaway: Edwardsson fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B (358M parameters once its vocabulary is cut) to predict a terminal's row edits per keypress, from 336k recorded sessions. On his own small tests, run once: 80 of 106 ShellBench commands exact (prompted base models 52, 60); self-repair plus more data took PresetBench from 24 to 38 of 47; parallel rows cut large-frame p95 latency from 6.7 s to 0.87 s.
verdict: Believe the engineering: clear, arithmetically sound, and matched by the demo's source. Read the accuracy as one author's small tests: memory is tested on the true history, so free-running drift is unmeasured, and self-repair's gain is mixed with extra data.
